Commands_Update: Report whether a newer build has been released. Never applies it — that restarts the server and disconnects everyone.
Commands_Credits: Print who made this and where to find them.
Commands_Shutdown: Ask the server to shut down gracefully, saving as it goes.
Server_Blurb: What the server is doing right now. Anything shown here that can be changed, can be changed here.
Server_Offline: Start the server to see what it is doing.
Server_MotdHint: Shown to every player as they enter. Line breaks become spaces.
Mod_Blurb: Every ban, kick, and mute currently in force, with the lift beside it. All three are held against the account, not the character, so lifting one frees every character on it.
Mod_HardwareBanModeSignal: This server REPORTS matches: a banned machine still gets in, and every moderator online is told. Change HardwareBans.Mode in serverconfig.json to refuse them instead.
Mod_HardwareBanModeBlock: This server REFUSES matches: a login or registration from one of these machines is turned away.
Mod_PenaltiesEmpty: No kick or mute is running.
Mod_NotLoaded: Nothing gathered yet. Refresh to read the ban list and sweep the accounts.
Bench_Blurb: Copies this server's world to a temporary folder, runs a second server on a free port, and connects fake players to it until the game thread runs out. The world you host is not touched, and no accounts are left behind.
Bench_Caveat: Every fake player walks four steps a second from the same spawn point, which is the heaviest thing this server does; a live world spreads people out and costs less. The fake players also run on this machine, so they compete with the server for cores. Both push the result down, never up.
Bench_Warning: Do not run this while people are playing. It takes cores away from the server they are on.
Bench_Booting: Waiting for the benchmark server to load…
Bench_BandLabel: with {Percent}% of the game thread spare
Bench_Reached: Reached {Peak} players with the game thread still keeping up. This machine was not the limit.
Bench_Saturated: The game thread ran out at {Peak} players.
Bench_JoinsFailed: The server stopped accepting players at {Peak}. Last reason: {Reason}
Bench_Dropped: Connections started dying at {Peak} players, which is worse than being refused.
Bench_Cancelled: Stopped before it finished. The steps below are still real.
Bench_Baseline: {Memory} with the world loaded and nobody on it
Bench_Cores: {Cores} cores, of which the simulation only ever uses one
Bench_MissedBeats: The benchmark missed {Count} of its own beats, so it applied less load than it claims. Treat these numbers as a floor.
Bench_Applied: Player limit set to {Players}. Save on the Configuration tab to keep it.
Bench_Unavailable: The benchmark measures the machine this window is on, so it needs a local server.
Commands_Blurb: Everything the server can be told to do. Each one runs exactly what you would type on the console, so the result appears there.
Commands_Moderation: List every ban, and every running kick or mute.
Commands_Unban: Lift a ban from an account.
Commands_Unkick: Lift a kick from an account.
Commands_Unmute: Lift a mute from an account, and from the live player.
Commands_HwBan: Ban the account AND the machine. The player must be online.
Commands_HwUnban: Lift every machine ban on an account.
Commands_Management: Remote operator access. Blank shows the port, token, and who is attached; "port" with a number rebinds now; "token" generates a new one; "off" stops listening.
Commands_Kick: Disconnect a player and keep them out for a while.
Commands_Mute: Stop a player speaking for a while.
Commands_Ban: Ban a player's account for good.
Commands_RefreshBanList: Reload the ban list from disk.
Commands_Motd: Set the message of the day.
Commands_Respawn: Reset one map's items and NPCs.
Commands_MapReport: List the map numbers nobody has authored yet.
Commands_AdvanceWar: Push war night into its next phase.
Console_StoppingNotice: Asked the server to shut down. It saves everything still in memory before it exits, so give it up to {Seconds} seconds.
Console_Rejected: The server refused the token. If you have retried a few times, the address is locked out for 5 minutes and even the right token is refused until it clears — wait, or restart the server. Run /management on the server to check the token length.
Console_IdentityChanged: {Host}:{Port} presented a different certificate than last time. Not attaching.
Console_ConnectionLost: The connection to the server ended.
Console_ShutdownBlocked: Not sent. This window cannot start a remote server back up, so use that server's own console if it has to go down.
Config_WindowGroupHint: Applies as soon as you change it.
Config_ServerGroupHint: Saved together, and applied the next time the server starts.
Config_SaveScope: Saves “{Group}” only. Everything above it applies as you change it. Changes take effect the next time the server starts.
Connection_Blurb: Which server this window drives. This setting belongs to this window, not to any server.
Connection_LaunchHint: Run the server installed beside this window, as a child process. Start and Stop control it directly.
Connection_AttachHint: Connect over the network, on this machine or another. Use localhost for a headless server running here. It has to have remote management turned on, and it keeps running when you detach.
Connection_TokenHint: The token that server was given. Kept in this window's own settings file so you are not retyping it.
Config_DeathPenaltyBlurb: What a player loses when they die. Each part is independent, and players under level 10 are spared either way.
Config_DurabilityLossHint: Worn equipment loses durability, and a caster loses reagents to match. Rain doubles it; a guild war doubles it again.
Config_ItemDropHint: Part of the bag falls on the ground. A player flagged for PK drops all of it, plus a chance at each worn piece.
Config_ExpLossHint: Death costs experience, and enough of it costs levels. Turning this off also means a PvP kill pays nothing, since that reward is taken from the victim.
Config_LanguageBlurb: The language this window, the server console, and the log files use. Players are not affected: each one sees the game in the language they chose.
Config_LanguageServerNote: This window changes straight away. The server console follows the next time it starts.
Hosting_Blurb: Where players connect, and where this server keeps its world.
Hosting_GameNameHint: What players see your game called, in their window title, menus, and HUD. A client ships with no name of its own — it wears the engine's until a server tells it this on connect. Leave it empty to keep the engine's name. It never affects file or folder names.
Hosting_GamePortHint: The port players type into their client. Only forward it on your router if they are outside your network.
Hosting_DataDirHint: Leave this empty to use the server's own data folder in your user profile. Point it somewhere else to keep a world on another drive, or in a folder you back up.
Hosting_WorldNameNote: A world folder can name itself in world.json. That name is yours, not the players' - it appears here and in the logs so you can tell a live world from a test copy, and never reaches anyone playing. What a player sees is the game's name.
Hosting_DataDirDefault: the server's data folder in your user profile
Hosting_MaxPlayersHint: How many people can be in the world at the same time. The right number depends on this machine, so measure it with the benchmark on the State tab rather than guessing.
Records_Blurb: How many of each kind of record this world has room for. Each one is a numbered slot the editor can author into, and the server creates the empty files on its next start. Lowering a number hides the slots above it; it does not delete the files.
Capacity_Blurb: What happens to the next person who tries to join once every slot is taken.
Capacity_ReservedHint: Held back from the general public so a Monitor or above can always get in and deal with whatever filled the server up. These come out of the limit above, so 20 players with 2 reserved lets 18 people in.
Capacity_QueueDepthHint: Everyone past this is turned away. Set it to 0 to refuse at the door instead, which is what the server did before it could queue. Waiting costs a connection and nothing else — nobody in the queue is using a slot.
Capacity_GraceHint: Seconds. A player who drops out keeps their place this long, so a network blip does not send them to the back. If their turn comes up while they are away, the slot waits for them too.
World_SpawnBlurb: The tile a new character is placed on, and where anyone without a purchased spawn point comes back after dying.
Schedule_Blurb: The weekly territory contest, in this machine's own time.
Schedule_WeekResetNote: The guild week rolls over the day after, on {Day}. Territory income, season weeks, and weekly quests all follow that boundary.
Logging_Blurb: What the server writes down, and how long it keeps it. Logs go to the logs folder beside the server.
Logging_LevelHint: How much the server records. Debug is everything; Warning and Error keep only what went wrong.
Logging_PacketsHint: Off by default, and worth leaving off: a busy server writes an enormous amount here. Turn them on to diagnose a connection problem. They have their own log file and never crowd the main one.
Logging_RetentionHint: Days. A new file is started each day; older ones are deleted past this count.
Logging_Unavailable: Some of these are not where they are expected in appsettings.json, so they are shown greyed out rather than overwritten. Restore the file's shape to edit them here.
Management_Blurb: Lets this server's console be reached from another machine, so you can watch it and run commands without being at the box.
Management_EnableHint: Both a port and a token are needed. Traffic is encrypted, and the token is the only thing standing between the port and your server's console, so treat it like a password.
Management_TokenHint: Give this to whoever attaches. Generate makes a fresh one; anyone still using the old token is cut off.
Management_LocalOnly: These settings belong to the server installed here. Attach locally to change them.
Config_RestartRequired: Changes apply the next time the server starts.
